AI for Networking & Networking for AI

Tiago Silva
NA-PRAIA

Using programmable networks to detect and recover from failures in GPU clusters, reducing interrupted training jobs and protecting model quality.

Luís Calado
GRAIL

Generating network protocol implementations from RFCs using AI, with developer feedback to resolve ambiguities and validate compliance with the standards.

Network & AI Security

André Pires
TITAN / Peregrine

Scaling ML-based traffic detection beyond switch memory limits through sketches, hierarchical flow-state management, and hybrid switch–SmartNIC architectures.

Miguel Pires
SpecSL

Making split learning more efficient with lightweight client-side speculation, conditional server offloading, and adaptive execution across heterogeneous devices.

Sérgio Olim
AEGIS / IRON

Designing adversarial attacks and defenses for AI-driven self-driving networks, with high-performance implementations on CPUs, GPUs, SmartNICs, and programmable switches.

João Andrade
NetDeception

Developing adaptive network deception that responds to attacker behaviour to delay reconnaissance and improve detection. In collaboration with Giorgios Spathoulas (NTNU).

Synthesis of Network Accelerators

António Delgado
BURST-TM

Designing a traffic manager for batch-oriented SmartNICs that groups and schedules packets for state locality and efficient processing. Co-advised with Muhammad Shahbaz (University of Michigan).

António Oliveira
VIP

Automatically transforming network functions into vectorized packet-processing pipelines, using program analysis to handle control flow and inter-packet dependencies.

Tiago Branquinho
BURST

Synthesizing accelerated network functions from high-level specifications, targeting batch processing, vectorized pipelines, and the RISC-V-based BURST SmartNIC.

Bernardo Boto
SPAIN

Automatically making stateful network functions easier to parallelize by restructuring shared counters and statistics into efficient per-core operations.
